drifted.spec_text: A background thread MUST call checkpoint() at a configurable interval (default 30 seconds). Note: the IExtentManager interface doc comment incorrectly states "five minutes" — the actual default is 30 seconds as set in the constructor.
drifted.actual: Code default is 30s (matches spec) via ExtentManager::new_inner, src/lib.rs:109-112. However, the spec's disclosure of the stale doc string covers only the trait doc comment in components/interfaces/src/iextent_manager.rs:244; README.md:12 independently repeats the same wrong '5 minutes' claim, which the spec does not mention.
drifted.location: components/extent-manager/README.md:12 (undisclosed second stale-doc site); components/extent-manager/src/lib.rs:109-112 (actual, correct default)

drifted.spec_text: The component supports a volatile_write_cache feature gate that controls whether BlockDeviceClient::flush() calls are issued to the metadata device. When enabled, flush calls in checkpoint and format paths are conditionally compiled out, improving performance on devices with volatile write caches where the caller accepts the associated durability risk.
drifted.actual: Polarity is inverted: the #[cfg(feature = "volatile_write_cache")] guard causes the flush() call to be compiled IN when the feature is enabled (and entirely absent/compiled-out by default) -- i.e. enabling the feature makes flushing happen, the opposite of 'compiled out'. Scope is also wrong: format() never calls flush() under any feature configuration; both feature-gated flush sites live in the checkpoint path only.

drifted.spec_text: Checkpoint coalescing limits concurrent checkpoint I/O to at most two active operations regardless of caller count.
drifted.actual: checkpoint_coalesce.in_progress is a bool, not a counter: at most ONE run_checkpoint() call is ever physically executing at any instant. The 'two' in the spec refers to the max number of sequential checkpoint rounds (completed_seq + 2) needed to satisfy a burst of waiting callers, not two concurrently-active I/O operations. As worded, this contradicts FR-015 ('at most one actual checkpoint I/O operation executes at a time... serializes all checkpoint I/O through a single writer'). README.md:13 repeats the same ambiguous phrasing.

Code matches the spec (FORMAT_VERSION: u32 = 6, src/superblock.rs:6), but README.md:19 still describes the on-disk format as 'format version (5)', stale from an earlier revision and inconsistent with both the spec and the code.

unspecced.feature: FormatParams.metadata_region_size and the shared metadata/data-device co-location mode (non-zero value shifts data_start_offset past the checkpoint regions so metadata and data can share one NVMe namespace)
unspecced.suggested_spec: New FR under 'Initialization & Format': document metadata_region_size semantics, default (128 MiB), and the data_start_offset computation when metadata and data coexist on one device.

unspecced.suggested_spec: New FR under 'Instance & Configuration': partition offset support for shared-namespace deployments.

unspecced.suggested_spec: New FR under 'Persistence & Recovery': post-checkpoint hook callback mechanism.

conflicts.description: FR-015 vs SC-006: FR-015 asserts single-writer serialization ('at most one actual checkpoint I/O operation executes at a time'), while SC-006 asserts 'at most two active operations' of 'concurrent checkpoint I/O'. The implementation (src/lib.rs:729-761) matches FR-015 exactly (a single in-flight boolean, never two concurrent checkpoints); SC-006's 'two' is only valid if reinterpreted as 'two sequential rounds to drain a burst of waiters', a materially different claim than what its own wording says. README.md inherits the same ambiguous phrasing.
